digest.component_or_area: CI lint infrastructure and store write sealing
propositions: Production bugs resulted from store write paths bypassing canonical write seams via raw git commands (add/commit/rm) in Python code and GitHub workflows.

A two-layer deterministic lint must flag raw git mutations in Python (AST-based, module-agnostic, tracking local list variables and opaque argv) and in workflows/shell (cwd-aware within-step, detecting tracker context via cd/.tickets-tracker, git -C, or working-directory).

Only two legitimate write seams exist: store internals (gitutil.run_git/run_git_write, event_append._run_git, txn/purge_bridge maintenance commands) and reconciler seam (git_adapter, _ref_lock), all others are bypasses or disposable sandbox fixtures.
Sanction is a single inline marker '# raw-git-ok: <reason>' with mandatory reason; marker-without-reason fails the lint, and no external allowlist file is used.
Report-mode bootstrap must enumerate all hits at first run; every hit is remediated or marked in the same PR, then enforcement mode is enabled, with tree clean at landing.

Lint teaches that store writes belong to event-append/transaction APIs or reconciler git_adapter, and covers git subcommand-position detection (add/commit/rm/reset/update-ref), variable-argv splat patterns (git_adapter, event_append idioms), and opaque-argv fail-closed forwarding (_ref_lock delegation shape).
